articles.summary: As AI-driven vulnerability discovery accelerates, the cybersecurity ecosystem is being forced to examine whether the standards, disclosure processes, and prioritization frameworks defenders rely on can still keep pace. In Rapid7’s new policy paper, understand where today’s vulnerability management infrastructure is breaking under AI-era conditions, and what governments, security companies, and frontier AI providers need to do next.
articles.title: Modernizing Global Vulnerability Standards For The Age Of AI

articles.summary: Metasploit is currently seeking user feedback on planned improvements to evasion capabilities via a proposal and feedback form that remains open until July 1, 2026. The latest update includes several new security modules, such as detection scanners for Audiobookshelf, LiteLLM Proxy, and Next.js, along with a new exploit module for Dalfox. Additionally, the release incorporates improvements to authentication brute-force modules and networking sockets, with further details and documentation available on the official Metasploit docsite.
articles.title: Weekly Metasploit Update: Modules for Audiobookshelf, LiteLLM, Next.js, Dalfox and more

articles.summary: Rapid7 has been named a Major Player in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide SIEM 2026 Vendor Assessment, the first IDC SIEM MarketScape to bring the enterprise and SMB markets into a single evaluation.
articles.title: Why SIEM is Moving Toward Unified Security Operations: Rapid7 Named a Major Player in IDC MarketScape

articles.summary: In a new episode of Experts on Experts, Rapid7 Executive Chairman Corey Thomas sits down with Sabeen Malik, VP of Global Government Affairs and Public Policy, to discuss a shift security leaders can’t afford to treat as separate threads: frontier AI, vulnerability discovery, cybersecurity compliance, and operational resilience.
articles.title: Experts on Experts: Why AI and Compliance Are Forcing A New Security Operating Model
